original_answer:
The paper's profiling features are text-based: they are used to identify accounts from their **way of writing tweets**, and are coupled with thematic and textual features to enhance the model's performance [1]. A specific example is the **Native Language Identification (NLI)** feature, which aims to detect IRA trolls by identifying their writing style in English tweets, exploiting that English tweets by non-native speakers exhibit different syntactic patterns [5]. The "Profiling Features" are also reported as an independent feature set in the classification results (separate from Network Features, theme-based features, etc.) [7].

Note that these profiling features should not be confused with the account metadata available in the Twitter-provided IRA dataset (profile description, account creation date, follower/followee counts, location, and account language); that dataset contains limited account details, and only the follower and followee counts were additionally used as a "Network Features" baseline [3].

cited_sources.text: Therefore, in this paper, we propose a text-based approach to detect the online trolls such as those that were discovered during the US 2016 presidential elections. Our approach is mainly based on textual features which uti- lize thematic information, and proﬁling features to identify the accounts from their way of writing tweets. We deduced the thematic information in a unsupervised way and we show that coupling them with the textual features enhanced the performance of the proposed model.

IRA dataset provided by Twitter contains less information about the ac- counts details, and they limited to: proﬁle description, account creation date, number of followers and followees, location, and account language. Therefore, as another baseline we use the number of followers and followees to assess their identiﬁcation ability (we will mention them as Network Features in the rest of the paper).

Thus, we propose the following features to identify these users using only their tweets text: – Native Language Identiﬁcation (NLI): This feature was inspired by earlier works on identifying native language of essays writers [22]. We aim to detect IRA trolls by identifying their way of writing English tweets. As shown in [31], English tweets generated by non-English speakers have a diﬀerent syntactic pattern .

We report the results of each feature set indepen- dently.
